chunks: And from him, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Yunus ibn Ya'qub, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'I fasted the month of Ramadan based on sighting [the moon] for twenty-nine days, and I did not complete [the full month of thirty].' He said to me, 'And I fasted it and did not complete [it].'

He then said to me, 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said, "The month is such-and-such."' And he showed with his fingers in both his hands, spreading his fingers like this and this and this and this and this and this, then he closed his thumb and gathered them [indicating thirty days].
He said, 'And his servant said to him while he was counting [the days], "I have seen the crescent moon." He said, "Go and inform them."'

key_terms.الشَّهْرُ شَهْرٌ كَذَا: The month is such-and-such (indicating a specific number, here thirty)
key_terms.قَبَضَ الْإِبْهَامَ: Closed/gathered the thumb (indicating the final count of thirty)

ai.seo_question: How many days are in the month of Ramadan according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the distinction between the lunar month's variable length (29 or 30 days) and the specific obligation of Ramadan, which is fixed at thirty days. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) uses the physical gesture of closing the thumb to indicate that while other months may be twenty-nine, Ramadan is completed only after thirty days, emphasizing the necessity of fulfilling the full count even if the initial sighting was on the 29th. This establishes a key jurisprudential principle in Shia fiqh regarding the completion of the fast when there is doubt about the month's length.
